summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 (FUSE and WinFsp Rust integration with grant-root awareness) using the GSD workflow tooling — research, plan, verify, and wave-based parallel execution — including recovering from a planner crash mid-phase and handling architectural blockers discovered during execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed for 14 plans (later expanded to 16) and committed; execution merged 10/14 plans (the full crates/core + crates/sdk foundation: Node codec/seal, gated listing, resumable rotation engine, revocation gap closures) green with cargo checks passing. The FUSE cutover cluster (69-09/10/13/14) was found architecturally unsound twice in a row — first for read/write path coupling, then for missing write-plane infrastructure entirely — resulting in a second re-scope that added two new additive plans (69-15, 69-16) which were planned and committed but not yet executed.

repo: The GSD commit helper reports `commit_failed` as a false-negative even when lint-staged/commit actually succeeds — always verify via `git log` before retrying or treating as a real failure.

API-SURFACE regen intel hook returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` for Rust phases since the extractor is TS/JS-focused — this is expected, not an error, and should be omitted from planner prompts in favor of RESEARCH.md symbol locations.

Fresh git worktrees lack `node_modules`, causing the husky pre-commit hook to fail (`lint-staged` not found) on the first commit attempt — fix is `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` inside the worktree, no code change needed.
`build_node_aad` (crates/core) fail-closes on non-UUID node IDs — test fixtures must use real UUIDv5 strings, tripped up multiple independent plans (69-06, 69-08).
Running rustfmt at the crate root inside a worktree can reformat unrelated files as a side effect — must diff/verify `git status --short` scope before committing to avoid stray drift.
`SentShareResponseDto` (apps/api) has no `revoked`/status field because shares are hard-deleted on revoke — every row returned by `GET /shares/sent` is inherently an active grant.

`crates/fuse` has zero references to `crates/sdk::listing` — it does raw IPNS resolves + IPFS fetches directly at ~10 call sites (content_ops, events, metadata, publish, fs, replay), so the gated read chain built in 69-06 was not actually consumable by FUSE without new adapter code.

No `build_node`/`create_node`/`publish_node` helper exists anywhere in crates/core or crates/sdk — the only `PublishedNode` producers were listing tests and the rotation engine (which only reseals existing nodes, never mints fresh ones).
The desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow's real name is "Desktop E2E Tests", not "CI E2E Tests" as the ROADMAP/CONTEXT worded it — `gh workflow run "CI E2E Tests"` would 404.
`seal_node` (crates/core) only seals the read-body; `PublishedNode.write_sealed` field exists in the struct but was never populated by any code path.
`parent_read_key: &[u8]` is passed as a borrow (not owned) in `rotate_one`, so the Rust type system itself — not just convention — prevents the terminal-owner zeroization rule from being violated.

code.finding: JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata welds the write journal to the legacy metadata type — this coupling was missed by every original FUSE-cutover plan and only surfaced during the second research pass.
has_covering_grant/maybe_rotate_on_scope_exit ported from TS packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/scope.ts; 16 tests including the SC#4/ROT-02 zero-rotation invariant.

rotate_one/rotate_read_from_node walk mechanics ported from TS engine.ts; later extended with verify_subtree_clean (crash-safe resume) and CRIT-1/HIGH-3/HIGH-4 revocation closures (content-key rotation, inner-grant re-mint, CAS-409 re-fetch-merge).
ResolvedChild/list_folder gated read entrypoint; the only NodeFetcher trait implementation was FakeFetcher (test-only) — no real production fetcher existed, discovered as a gap during P1 execution.

workflow: When a spawned planner agent crashes mid-response but has written partial output to disk, verify what actually landed (frontmatter validity, `</output>` closure) before deciding whether to resume with a fresh single-plan-mode planner rather than restarting the whole phase.
GSD role-separation: even during error recovery, the orchestrator should spawn a fresh planner agent to author a missing plan rather than writing plan content inline itself.

Canary pattern: execute the first plan of the first wave synchronously (not backgrounded) to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo-gate pipeline before fanning out later waves in parallel — caught nothing here but was worth the validation given `--auto` unattended execution.

Worktree agent-reported `expected_base` metadata can be a mis-capture (the agent's own docs commit instead of the true fork point) — always verify the actual merge-base via git before recording/merging to avoid a bad merge.
ScheduleWakeup plus a durable handoff scratchpad file let the session pause for 40 minutes and resume with full recovery state even if context gets summarized in between.

When an executor agent hits a genuine architectural/Rule-4 deviation, it should make zero file edits, not write a SUMMARY.md, and return a structured blocker for the orchestrator to replan — rather than guessing destructively.

friction: Planner agent crashed mid-response (API connection closed) while writing the final plan (69-14), losing the in-flight summary though 13 of 14 plans were already safely on disk.

The crashed planner used internal pseudo-IDs (SC-01..SC-06) in plan `requirements:` frontmatter instead of the actual roadmap requirement ID TEST-03, which would have failed the §13 coverage gate silently if not caught.
Commit helper repeatedly reported `commit_failed` as a false-negative across multiple steps, requiring manual `git log` verification each time to confirm work actually landed.

Plan 69-09 (FUSE read-path ECIES→symmetric swap) discovered mid-execution that the named call sites are reachable from ~9 additional files outside its scope, and that the write path was never migrated off legacy types — invalidating both itself and the downstream 69-10 (D-04 legacy-type deletion) plan.

After a full research+replan cycle produced a supposedly-atomic P1 (69-09) cutover plan, the opus executor discovered on a second attempt that the underlying write-plane emit API and read adapter infrastructure didn't exist at all — a second, deeper architectural scope gap requiring yet another research+replan round (P1a: 69-15/69-16).

Original phase 69 scoping substantially underestimated the FUSE/WinFsp cutover complexity — the web equivalent took ~5 phases (62–65 write-plane + 68.2 read consolidation) worth of subsystem work compressed into what was planned as tail-end plans of one phase.
open_items: P1a plans (69-15 core write-body codec, 69-16 sdk emit+read-adapter) are planned, committed, and approved-pending but not yet executed.
69-09 (P1b, atomic FUSE consumer cutover) now depends on 69-01, 69-04, 69-06, 69-15, 69-16 and has not been re-attempted since the write-plane gap was found.
69-10 (P2, delete legacy core types) and 69-13 (P3, grant-gated write path + SC#2/D-07) remain unexecuted, blocked behind P1b.
69-14 (P4, WinFsp/Windows + TEST-03) is `autonomous: false` and requires the user's physical Windows machine — the designated hard hand-off point of the phase.
The SC#6 grep-gate in 69-06/69-09 still uses a placeholder crate-private symbol name per the plan-checker's non-blocking warning; needs confirmation with the real symbol at execution/build time.

The pre-existing SHARE-WRITE-KEY gap (write-share key threading, from prior session memory) has not been revisited and may interact with the new D-07 write-body/writeKey plane being built in 69-15/69-16.
